CS0103.explanation: The compiler reached a name it does not know. In C# every name must be declared before it is used - a variable, a method, or a using for its namespace.
CS0103.cause: A spelling mistake, or using a variable outside the braces it was declared in.

CS1002.explanation: A semicolon is missing at the end of a statement.
CS1002.cause: A forgotten semicolon - usually at the end of the line BEFORE the one named.

CS1525.explanation: The compiler expected a value at that spot and found something that cannot be one.
CS1525.cause: An expression left unfinished, such as an assignment with nothing on the right.
CS1525.example:
int x = ;    // nothing to assign
int x = 0;

CS0029.explanation: A value of one type was put where a different type is required, and C# will not convert it for you.
CS0029.cause: Assigning text to a number variable, or forgetting to convert.
CS0029.example:
int age = "12";                // text into a number
int age = int.Parse("12");     // convert first

CS0161.explanation: A method promises to return a value and there is a path through it that returns nothing.
CS0161.cause: A return inside an if with no return for the other case.

CS0165.explanation: A local variable is read before anything has been stored in it. C# will not guess a starting value.
CS0165.cause: Declaring a variable and assigning it only inside an if that might not run.

CS0117.explanation: The type exists, but it has no member with that name.
CS0117.cause: A spelling or capitalisation mistake - C# member names always start with a capital letter.
CS0117.example:
Console.writeline("hi");   // lower case w and l
Console.WriteLine("hi");

CS1061.explanation: The value has no method or property with that name. The value is not the kind of thing you thought it was.
CS1061.cause: Calling a List method on an array, or a string method on a number.

CS0246.explanation: The compiler cannot find that type or namespace anywhere.
CS0246.cause: A missing using line, or a spelling mistake in the type name.
CS0246.example:
List<int> nums = new();               // needs the collections namespace
using System.Collections.Generic;     // add this at the top

CS0019.explanation: An operator was used with types it does not work on - such as subtracting one piece of text from another.
CS0019.cause: Doing arithmetic on values that are still text.

CS0136.explanation: A name is declared twice in overlapping scopes, so it is not clear which one a use refers to.
CS0136.cause: Declaring a variable inside a loop or an if with the same name as one outside it.

CS5001.explanation: The program has no starting point. A C# program needs a Main method, or top-level statements in one file.
CS5001.cause: Every line is inside a class with no Main, or the entry file is not the one being built.

NullReferenceException.explanation: Something used a dot on a variable holding null. null means "no object at all", so there is nothing to ask.
NullReferenceException.cause: A variable that was never given an object, or a lookup that found nothing.

IndexOutOfRangeException.explanation: You asked for a position that does not exist. An array of 3 has positions 0, 1 and 2.
IndexOutOfRangeException.cause: Counting from 1 instead of 0, or a loop using <= where < was meant.

FormatException.explanation: Text was converted to a number and the text was not a number.
FormatException.cause: int.Parse on input containing letters, spaces, or nothing at all.
FormatException.example:
int.Parse("twelve");
int.TryParse("twelve", out int n);   // returns false instead of failing

DivideByZeroException.explanation: A whole number was divided by zero, which has no answer.
DivideByZeroException.cause: A count or a length that turned out to be 0.
DivideByZeroException.example:
int average = total / count;   // count is 0
if (count != 0) average = total / count;

InvalidOperationException.explanation: The operation is fine in general but not valid right now, in the state the object is in.
InvalidOperationException.cause: First() on an empty collection, or changing a collection while looping over it.
InvalidOperationException.example:
var first = items.First();            // empty collection
var first2 = items.FirstOrDefault();  // gives null instead of failing

StackOverflowException.explanation: A method called itself over and over until there was no room left to remember the calls.
StackOverflowException.cause: A recursive method whose stopping condition is missing or never reached.
StackOverflowException.example:
int Count(int n) => Count(n - 1);                 // never stops
int CountOk(int n) => n <= 0 ? 0 : CountOk(n - 1);
